entityDescription:
ReLUIS 
 
Competence Center of the Civil Protection Department - decree of the Department Chief n.3152 of 24 July 2013, published on the Gazzetta Ufficiale n. 220 of 19 September 2013
 
The Laboratories University Network of seismic engineering (Rete dei Laboratori Universitari di Ingegneria Sismica - ReLUIS), founded through a conventional act signed on the 17th of April of 2003, is a interuniversity consortium with the purpose to co-ordinate the activity of earthquake engineering University Laboratories, giving scientific, organizational, technical and financial supports to associated University while promoting their participation to scientific and technological-orientated activities in earthquake engineering field, in accordance with national and international research plans in this area.
Co-ordination action promotes the partnerships between Universities, Private Universities, and Inter-university Centres (henceforth indicated with the term “University”) and between them and other Research Institutes and Industries and also promotes the development of earthquake engineering Laboratories according to its statute, through conducting generation and dissemination of knowledge.
The consortium is a scientific interlocutor of different Governmental, Regional, Provincial and Council Agencies and of public and private Institutes to get tangible objectives concerning vulnerability and risk evaluation and reduction.
All the scholars belonging to the associated consortium structures, at the moment of acknowledgment to the consortium or belonging to the foundation for founder members, that take care of problems concerning seismic engineering, can associate and participate in Consortium activities by co-operating in an interdisciplinary way.
The consortium has the main office in Naples in the Department of Structures for Engineering and Architecture, University of Naples “Federico II”. The consortium is a nonprofit organization.
Founder and pertaining members are:
University of Basilicata (Dep. of Structures, Geotechnical and Engineering Geology)
University of Naples Federico II (Dep. of Civil Engineering and Architecture)
University of Pavia (Dep. of Civil, Environmental and Mechanical Engineering)
Successive members:
University of Trento (Dip. of Civil, Environmental and Mechanical Engineering)
In addition to partner universities, experts and professors belonging to further universities and research institutes, well widespread on the national territory, as shown in the figure below, participate to the research and support activities of the Consortium.

entityDescription: The Stochastic Hydrogeology Lab is a research unit within the Faculty of Sciences of the University of Neuchâtel. It develops mathematical methods and software in the field of spatio-temporal statistics. These methods are used to interpolate properties based on observations and quantify uncertainty. This team is among the world leader in the field of multiple-point statisticis, which is a branch of spatial statistics that build models by learning from example. It is a category of machine learning method able to produce patterns in space or time that are similar to those observed in analog data. These methods can be used to reconstruct the spatial distribution of rock types in the undeground, fill missing data gaps in remote sensing observation, or model time series.

entityDescription:
YPlasma is an innovative enterprise that emerged from the prestigious Instituto Nacional de Técnica Aeroespacial (INTA), established as a spin-off in February 2024. YPlasma's core offering is its patented plasma actuator technology, originally developed for space propulsion, which it aims to adapt for a variety of earth-based uses.
Their business model is built on a licensing strategy that allows for broad utilization of their technology. This flexibility and customizability mean that YPlasma can form partnerships across different sectors, where its technology can be tailored to specific industrial needs. The company's strategy ensures quick technology dissemination and adaptation, which is key for the collaborative growth of both YPlasma and its partners.
The hallmark of YPlasma's technology is its space-derived legacy, which guarantees robustness and versatility—qualities that are vital in the extreme environment of space. Bringing this technology down to earth, YPlasma has chosen to focus initially on the wind energy sector. Their technology addresses major challenges in wind turbines, such as icing and aerodynamic inefficiency, promising to increase energy yield and reliability. Key pilot projects like the partnership with Sotavento wind park (owned by Enel and Iberdrola) serve as a proving ground for their technology's capabilities, demonstrating real-world benefits. Additional agreements with Enel Green Power, NextEra Energy, Total Energies and Plenium Partners are in place to test the technology.
YPlasma is led by CEO David Garcia, who has a 15-year background in leading hard tech and sustainability startups, Antonio Conesa, Head of Aerodynamics at INTA and Mario Sanchez, CTO and co-authors of the patent, bring a deep expertise in aerodynamics and plasma technology research, with a track record of significant breakthroughs.
The versatility of YPlasma's plasma actuators stretches well beyond the wind energy industry. For satellites, they offer a maintenance-free and efficient propulsion system alternative for low-orbits, protected against extreme space temperatures.
In the aviation sector, these actuators can dramatically improve aerodynamic efficiency, leading to significant fuel savings and emission reductions. We have been selected by Airbus as their prime choice following an extensive evaluation of over 80 technologies. Additionally, they can play a pivotal role in thermal management for high-stakes applications in data centers, automotive, and energy storage industries, enhancing safety, performance, and longevity. YPlasma also ventures into agriculture, where their technology promotes sustainable plant growth and offers a method for chemical-free environmental sanitization.
As YPlasma builds on its initial successes in the wind energy pilots and seeks opportunities in other sectors, it aims to serve as a model of innovation, utilizing the transformative capabilities of plasma actuator technology to push various industries towards a more efficient, sustainable future.

YPlasma also ventures into agriculture, where their technology promotes sustainable plant growth and offers a method for chemical-free environmental sanitization.
As YPlasma builds on its initial successes in the wind energy pilots and seeks opportunities in other sectors, it aims to serve as a model of innovation, utilizing the transformative capabilities of plasma actuator technology to push various industries towards a more efficient, sustainable future.

AquaCloud was established in 2017 and is a big data project anchored in the aquaculture industry’s need to solve common challenges in order to create sustainable growth.
The project is part of NCE Seafood Innovation and began together with cluster members Lerøy Seafood Group ASA, Grieg Seafood ASA, Mowi ASA, Bremnes Seashore AS, Lingalaks AS, Eide Fjordbruk, and Bolaks AS. The project has developed substantially since 2017, and today the project involve a even broader group of leading aquaculture companies.

In 2021, the project was spun out of the cluster and is now an limited company. 
The initial scope of this groundbreaking initiative was to establish a secure database for storing data and to use advanced analytics to identify where sea lice outbreaks were probable. This part of the project celebrated some success. However, data quality and dependability were insufficient to reach the ambitious goals at the time.
At the core of the project is still the Data Platform which receives continuous updates from participating companies and represents a unique repository of high-resolution data from their farming operations. While observing obvious legal and competitive limitations, selected datasets will be shared both between participants and even made generally available to third parties for innovation.
The project has evolved from being a pure sea lice forecasting asset to become a hub of industry activities including companies from multiple sectors in the industry. Based on the initial findings of lacking data quality, the project launched several workflows addressing standardization needs in the industry:
- Sensor Data – an open IoT-based standard allowing equal access to aquaculture sensors and systems
- Fish Health – common standards for areas such as mortality causes and fish group identification as well as digital information exchange between various health and welfare entities
- Environmental Data – reviewed the environmental section of NS9417 standard on unambiguous terminology and methods for documentation of production

Leanspace is a leading provider of ground segment solutions. 
Satellites have become so critical that our societies can no longer function without them. Yet each satellite requires a complex and costly infrastructure on the ground, and even today it takes years to build them. Forecasts show that space will grow strongly, bringing new solutions to the problems we face on Earth. At Leanspace we believe that for this to happen, space programs need to be radically simpler to execute than they are today. Space is an antiquated industry in dire need of digital disruption.We founded Leanspace in 2020 with two value propositions in mind. The first is to reduce the costs, time and risks involved in setting up ground segments. The second, to increase the agility and resilience of space missions, through more flexible ground infrastructures. These are made possible by our unique technology, a modular, cloud-native software platform that we've been developing for 4 years now. 
Today, our technology has been proven in orbit (TRL9). With it, we offer products and solutions that cover every link in the operational value chain: control centers, antenna integration, cloud deployment, cybersecurity...Our platform is agnostic, so it can be used for any type of space vehicle: Earth observation, satellite communications, launchers, but also for life extension, refuelling or de-orbiting operations...

Located in Salzburg, Austria, eoVision GmbH is an SME providing products and services related to satellite remote sensing data. The company was founded in 2008 based on the extensive expertise of its founders in the fields of satellite remote sensing applications and publishing for infotainment/edutainment.
The offered services range from consultancy in the context of satellite data acquisition and application, and support in the acquisition of appropriate data, to the preparation, evaluation and interpretation of data following the specific information requirements of the customer.
Among the products, coffee-table books, atlases and maps based on satellite data are most important. The book series "Human Footprint" provides well-selected examples highlighting the status and changes of the planet. Special educational products such as a school atlas produced for ESA and exhibitions provided to museums and science centers complete eoVision's product portfolio. In all these products, the company's goal is to combine attractive contents and stories with highest quality of presentation, i.e. processing of the satellite data.

Vodafone Greece is a member of the Vodafone Group, one of the largest telecommunications groups in the world, and acts as a catalyst in the Greek market. With unique know-how and talented human resources, Vodafone invests in the most modern and future-proof digital infrastructure, reliably supports the needs of individuals and businesses and actively contributes to economic and social development in the country. In its 26 years of activity in Greece, Vodafone leads the market forward and continues to contribute to innovation, implementing a strategic plan for investments of €500 million. by 2020. Earlier, from 2008 to 2015, Vodafone invested more than €1.5 billion. euro in Greece. Vodafone Greece has one of the largest private optical networks in Greece, covering more than 9,000 km. and serves more than 850,000 broadband connections. At the same time, it has more than 3,000 facilities providing high capacity lines (fiber to the building). Today, Vodafone proceeds with the first large-scale implementation of fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) networks in Greece. In this context, the company completed the development of a new generation network (also using fiber optics) in Freattida, Neos Kosmos, Pagrati, Nursing Home and Nea Ionia and continues in the coming months the implementation of new generation networks (FTTH or FTTC) in many areas of Athens, Thessaloniki, Volos, Kozani, Ioannina and Veria and in a total of 25 centers. At the same time, the company is constantly expanding its telecommunications network in mobile, with extensive 3G and 4G coverage and 5G services that offer high speeds, quality and reliability to its subscribers. Vodafone is recognized as an experienced partner that supports every modern need for communication with quality solutions and an excellent service experience. Vodafone provides the most reliable and quality Internet access, for corporate use, through its own digital leased circuits, using microwave links or fiber optics. The main feature of this service, which differentiates it from other providers, is the provision and support of Internet access and the relevant leased circuit from the same provider, which makes Vodafone a one-stop-shop. Vodafone's policy to manage risks and opportunities in a systematic manner and to aim at the continuous improvement and satisfaction of the needs of all stakeholders, led it to develop an integrated management system. At Vodafone we have been certified by Lloyd's Register Quality Assurance (LRQA): 
• Quality Management according to ISO 9001:2015 for activity related to the subject of the declaration, with scope in the design, development, implementation, operation, maintenance and monitoring of mobile and fixed communication networks, wireless technologies and data networks. 
• Environmental Management according to ISO 14001:2015 for an activity related to the subject of the declaration, with scope in design, development, implementation, Operation, maintenance and surveillance of mobile and fixed communication networks, wireless technologies and data networks. 
• Management of Occupational Health and Safety according to ISO 45001:2018 for an activity related to the subject of this Declaration, with scope in the design, development, implementation, operation, maintenance and monitoring of mobile and fixed communication networks, wireless technologies and data networks. 
Vodafone also has the following certifications: 
• Information Security Management according to ISO/IEC 27001:2013 
• Business Continuity Management according to ISO 22301:2012 
• Energy Management according to ISO 50001:2018
